note: The real Next route at apps/web/src/app/api/webhooks/privy/route.ts, running under `pnpm dev` on http://localhost:3000, POSTed by hand. SIMULATED: the delivery — this environment has no public URL, so Privy itself cannot call the endpoint, and the webhook signing key is a locally generated svix key rather than one issued by a registered Privy endpoint. REAL: the routing, the raw-body handling, and `privy.webhooks().verify` — the tampered signature is rejected with 401 before the body is parsed or the database touched. The correctly signed request passes verification and proceeds to Postgres, which is unreachable from this sandbox, so it fails there (see the body). The full split against this same handler, with PGlite standing in for Postgres, is in phase3-split.json.
